label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration, drop-off

Last month I told Dana I would write this up once my writer had been through a real trial. It has now done eight days of a civil trial, so here it is.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3.

Work done: Full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and the internal battery replaced. I asked for the recalibration, a number bar sensor inspection, the cleaning and the firmware. The battery came up while she had it open. It was holding about 60% of rated capacity. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

Dropped off: Monday, October 19.
Returned: Tuesday, October 27. That is six business days against the ten they quoted.

Quoted: $285.00.
Paid: $310.00. The extra $25 was the battery, parts and labor. Gloria Ruark, the technician, emailed me about it and said she would not go ahead without my approval. She waited until I said yes. I care about that more than the $25. I have had shops add things and tell me at the counter.

Paid personally, as I do with all my equipment. No reimbursement from the court.

Loaner: Yes, a Stenvale Aria 2. Its tilt arm would not hold position. It slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I mentioned it in my reply about the battery, and Gloria wrote back that they would repair it before it goes out again. If you take a loaner, set it up at home and check the tilt before you rely on it.

The shop: Harbor Point is a two-person operation off York Road. Parking in back is free. When I picked up the machine it came with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment made. In all my years nobody has ever given me that, and I have kept it in the case.

How it has held up: My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks almost entirely in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke that day, and it hasn't since. The recalibration feels even across the board, and I have had no trouble with the new firmware so far.

The weakness: the phone. Their line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. I called on Wednesday the 21st to ask how things were going. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box to leave a message in. Gloria emailed me the next day, and by email she has been prompt and clear every time. Still, if you work a Monday docket, or you are the kind of reporter who needs an answer on a Friday about whether your machine will be ready for Monday, you cannot count on reaching anyone by phone. Plan around it. Ask your questions at drop-off, get the technician's email, and use that.

Dana, to answer what you asked: yes, I would trust them with your Aria. The double-stroking on the number bar is exactly what they fixed on mine. They replaced the sensor rather than just adjusting it, and the fix has held through a hard week of testimony. Turnaround beat the estimate, the price was fair for the work, and they asked before adding anything. Just don't expect to reach them by phone on a Monday or a Friday. Use email. And check the loaner before you need it.

I will use them again.

Maureen
